title: Stalk comparison for the naive cotangent complex of sheaves of rings
statement:
Let $T$ be a topological space and $\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ a homomorphism of sheaves of commutative rings on its small site of opens, with sizes in the chosen universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $K=\mathrm{NL}_{\mathcal B/\mathcal A}$ be the standard two-term sheaf complex $K_{\mathcal B}$ of [lem-sfb-sheaf-polynomial-cotangent-comparison], and let $t\in T$. Stalks and germs are those of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. For a map $A\to B$ of commutative rings, write $C_{B/A}=[I/I^2\to B\otimes_{A[B]}\Omega_{A[B]/A}]$ in degrees $-1,0$, where $A[B]=A[x_b\mid b\in B]$, $I=\ker(A[B]\to B)$, and $[h]\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dh$; this is the naive complex of [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] written cohomologically, using [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$K_t\simeq C_{\mathcal B_t/\mathcal A_t}\quad\text{in }D(\mathcal B_t)$$
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. It is induced by the canonical comparison from the stalk of the standard sheaf complex to the standard complex of stalk rings. More precisely, for every open $W\ni t$, compose the sectionwise map $C_{\mathcal B(W)/\mathcal A(W)}\to K(W)$ with the germ map to $K_t$. After the displayed comparison its image in $D(\mathcal B_t)$ is the map induced by the two germ ring maps $\mathcal A(W)\to\mathcal A_t$, $\mathcal B(W)\to\mathcal B_t$: coefficients go to their germs, $x_b\mapsto x_{b_t}$, kernel classes $[h]\mapsto[h_t]$, and $b\otimes\mathrm dh\mapsto b_t\otimes\mathrm d(h_t)$. Here maps to $\mathcal B_t$-complexes are extended from the source coefficient ring when necessary. The comparison is natural for homomorphisms of ring sheaves. No finiteness or separation condition on $T$ is assumed.

proof.text: Let i:{t}→T be the continuous inclusion of the one-point space, with its site of opens. The inverse-image adjunction and preservation of finite limits in [lem-weil-pbc-sets-inverse-image-colimits-finite-products] make this a geometric morphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk], i^{-1}F on its unique nonempty open is canonically F_t, for ring sheaves and abelian sheaves, and the unit sends a section to its germ. A sheaf on a point is determined by its value on that open (its value on the empty open is terminal), so this identifies ring and abelian sheaves there with rings and abelian groups. For modules the same identification is linear: the multiplication of inverse-image local representatives in [def-pc-topological-inverse-image-module] gives (rs)_t=r_t s_t, exactly the action in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Thus i^{-1}K is the termwise stalk complex K_t with its B_t-module structure.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-topos-naive-cotangent-pullback] to this geometric morphism and A→B. Its sites are small in the chosen universe, and its conclusion concerns termwise inverse image of the standard complex, so no derived tensor product or flatness hypothesis is needed. On the point its target standard complex is C_{B_t/A_t}: evaluating the sheaf polynomial, kernel, conormal quotient and differential module on the unique nonempty open gives precisely the ring construction. Its canonical identifications therefore give K_t≃C_{B_t/A_t} in D(B_t). In particular this is the comparison induced by those identifications, not a choice of an unrelated isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0D09 (lemma-stalk-NL), proof via lemma-pullback-NL; section-netherlander, standard construction and equation-commutative-square-sheaves.

proof.text: We identify the map just obtained. For W containing t, the unit description in [lem-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image-stalk] sends every coefficient a to a_t and every generator b to b_t. Hence the canonical polynomial identification in [lem-sfb-topos-naive-cotangent-pullback] sends x_b to x_{b_t}, by the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. It commutes with evaluation, so h in the sectionwise evaluation kernel maps to h_t in the stalk evaluation kernel, and its conormal class maps to [h_t]. The differential identification sends dh to d(h_t), by the universal derivation of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Its tensor identification consequently sends b⊗dh to b_t⊗d(h_t). These formulas give the asserted composite from the sectionwise complex, since the map to the standard sheaf complex of [lem-sfb-sheaf-polynomial-cotangent-comparison] is induced by the same polynomial, quotient and differential maps. They commute with the differential: the image of 1⊗dh is 1⊗d(h_t), the differential of [h_t].

source.place: Tag 0D09 (lemma-stalk-NL), proof via lemma-pullback-NL; section-netherlander, standard construction and equation-commutative-square-sheaves.

proof.text: For a commutative square A→B, A'→B' of ring sheaves, both composites in the naturality square send a coefficient a to the germ of its image, x_b to x_{image(b)_t}, [h] to [image(h)_t], and b⊗dh to image(b)_t⊗d(image(h)_t). Naturality of germs [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and the polynomial universal property [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] give equality on polynomials; quotient classes and the generating differentials and tensors give equality in both degrees. Thus the comparison is a natural chain map. Its image under localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] has the claimed naturality and sectionwise compatibility in D(B_t), with scalar extension understood as in the statement. Only the singleton inclusion and open neighbourhoods were used, so there is no separation or finiteness assumption on T.
